content.tldr: Iceberg coordinates concurrent writes using Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) and atomic Compare-And-Swap (CAS) catalog operations, automatically retrying non-conflicting commits.
content.simple_explanation: When a writer begins a transaction, it reads the current table snapshot base. It writes new data and manifest files independently. When ready to commit, it attempts an atomic Compare-And-Swap (CAS) update in the catalog (e.g. in DynamoDB, JDBC, or Hive). If another writer committed first, the CAS fails. Iceberg then checks whether the two commits actually conflict: if Writer A appended partition '2026-10-31' and Writer B appended '2026-11-01', Iceberg re-bases Writer B's commit on top of A and retries automatically without failing the job.
content.real_world_example: Collaborative document editing: two users simultaneously edit different paragraphs in a shared online document; the system seamlessly merges both edits without rejecting either contributor's work.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: True conflicts occur when two concurrent writers attempt to mutate or delete the exact same data files (e.g. concurrent MERGE operations). In this scenario, Iceberg throws a CommitFailedException to protect data integrity, requiring application retry.
